title: Planning and Zoning Commission Meeting
location: 1670 Naturita St, Norwood CO 81423
summary: Norwood's Planning and Zoning Commission meets November 16 at 6:30 p.m. at Town Hall. The substantive work is on two fronts that tend to shape everything else: a Land Use Code update and a Master Plan update — the kind of foundational documents that determine what gets built where for years to come. The commission also takes up a discussion of the Board of Adjustments, which handles variance requests and sits at the intersection of the code and how it actually gets applied on the ground.

title: Board of County Commissioners
location: Ouray County 4-H Event Center, 22739 Highway 550, Ridgway, CO 81432
summary: A substantive session for the Ouray County BOCC. Two resolutions stand out: Resolution 2026-031 repeals the county's austerity measures (Resolution 2026-008), signaling a shift in the county's fiscal posture; and Resolution 2026-032 adopts a formal AI policy and governance standards — one of the first such moves in the region. The 2027 budget gets an update and discussion, followed by a public hearing on amending the 2026 budget via Resolution 2026-033. On the infrastructure side, commissioners take up a change order on the Corbett Creek project, a runoff concern on CR-361's upper bridge, and an OHV grant application for an Alpine Ranger Program through Colorado Parks and Wildlife. Human Services business includes MOUs with CASA and an IGA with Montrose County for child support services. Executive session covers active water and civil litigation — dockets dating back to 2019 — plus potential code enforcement action for unpermitted structures and road closures in the McIntyre Gulch high alpine area, and a possible property transaction at 800 N. Oak Street in Ouray.

title: Town Council
location: Hybrid/Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The big item this meeting is the 2027 budget — Council takes it to a vote alongside the property tax levy that funds it. Woven into that same session: second reading of an ordinance suspending the 5% Open Space Fund dedication from Real Estate Transfer Tax revenue for the 2027 budget year, a recurring tension between fiscal pressure and the land-conservation commitments voters have long expected. Also on second reading: amendments to the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program (TEMP), with a companion action item updating TEMP's energy offset fee calculator. The morning work sessions carry weight too — a 60-minute discussion on establishing a sewer authority is the kind of infrastructure governance question that tends to reshape how utilities are managed and funded for years. An extended producer responsibility update covers the state's new composting mandate and what local curbside service might look like. A Canyonlands/Tower House project update appears in the manager's report. Two executive sessions close the day: one on open space property interests, one on town facilities.

title: (Master Lease Lottery) Telluride Housing Authority
location: Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: The Telluride Housing Authority meets to conduct two Master Lease Lottery drawings — one for the Telluride Boarding House at 1100 Black Bear Rd and one for the Virginia Placer IIA Apartments at 1280 Black Bear Rd. Both drawings proceed under Employee Rental Housing Policies §107 and 707.2. For anyone waiting on workforce housing up on Black Bear Road, this is the meeting that determines who gets in.

title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session
location: Ouray County 4-H Event Center, 22739 Highway 550, Ridgway, CO 81432
summary: A work session, so no formal votes — but the direction commissioners give here shapes what comes back for action later. The morning opens with EMS director Nathan McCullough's quarterly update and a discussion of an intergovernmental agreement between the county and Ridgway Fire. Then come two memoranda of understanding: one with the City of Ouray at 10:00, one with the Town of Ridgway at 10:30 — the specifics of each aren't spelled out in the agenda, but MOUs with both municipal neighbors in the same session suggests coordinated service or cost-sharing conversations are in motion. The afternoon wraps with commissioner and administrative reports, then 2027 budget discussion picks up wherever it left off the previous day.

title: HARC Meeting
location: Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: A heavy agenda for November 18. The two items that have been waiting since August — the Shandoka Lot redevelopment preliminary large-scale reviews for Buildings 1 & 2 and Buildings 3 & 4 at 860 Black Bear Rd — are finally being heard, with the Town of Telluride as applicant and Design Workshop doing the design work. Both involve new construction outside the historic district exceeding 5,000 sq ft in an Accommodations 2 zone. Also on the docket: preliminary large-scale reviews for two other Town-owned sites — 113 W Columbia (Rebekah Hall itself, demolition of the existing principal structure plus new construction over 5,000 sq ft) and 335 W Colorado (demolition of a THAS-rated primary structure, large-scale new construction, and relocation of two historic sheds). A privately owned property at 421 E Columbia gets a small-scale addition and minor alterations. The two 238 N Pine applications are continued without discussion to April 21, 2027. HARC also elects its chair and vice chair and reviews its 2026 annual report.

title: Town Council Meeting
location: Town Hall, 455 Mountain Village Blvd, Suite A
summary: A full agenda this Thursday. The budget cycle is front and center: Council opens a public hearing on the Mountain Village Metro District's proposed 2027 budget, then takes up first readings on both the 2027 Town budget ordinance and the 2026 property tax levy ordinance, followed by adoption of the 2027 fee schedules. On the land use side, a minor subdivision for Lots 640A and OSP-35-A gets a resolution vote. Items 14 and 15 — a height variance and vested property right for a single-family home on Lot 98 — are both continued to January. Two work sessions carry real weight: one on the draft sewer authority agreement between Mountain Village and Telluride for a new regional wastewater treatment plant, and one checking in on the Rural Homes Ilium affordable housing feasibility study. Council also considers a letter of support for the Colorado Association of Ski Towns' 2027 legislative agenda, votes on a Public Art Commission appointment, and reviews third-quarter financials. The evening closes with an executive session on the ongoing Sunset Concert litigation.

title: Planning & Zoning Commission
location: Hybrid/Rebekah Hall, 113 W Columbia Ave
summary: A light agenda for this one. The 222 West San Juan Avenue subdivision work session — which had been continued from October — has since been withdrawn by the applicant, so it won't be heard. The commission will get a presentation on wildfire modeling technologies from Firebird Chief Scientist Jason Sibold, and continue a work session on potential Land Use Code amendments to landscaping requirements (LUC 3-502) and tree maintenance and removal rules (LUC 3-505). The board will also elect a new chair and vice chair, hear about the December 3 Comprehensive Plan community engagement session, and review the draft 2027 meeting calendar.
